evidence: Quint. 1.4.27: ut ignōret genera et quālitātēs et persōnās et numerōs
terms.comment: Varro gives the three: the one who speaks, the one spoken to, the one spoken of. First person is prīma persōna (Quint. 1.6.15), second secunda, third tertia; the question is Cujus persōnae est? (Traupman 238).

phrases.latin: quom item persōnārum nātūra triplex esset, quī loquerētur, ad quem, dē quō
phrases.english: since the nature of persons was likewise threefold: who was speaking, to whom, about whom

phrases.latin: nam praeteritō quidem tempore variē fōrmārī verba prīmā persōnā o litterā terminata, ipsa analogia cōnfiteātur
phrases.english: for analogy itself would admit that verbs ending in o in the first person form their perfect in various ways
What person is it? — First person.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 226, 238, 240, 248.
